about: Shared parity vectors for the Rust mutation-log STEP writer (#5941).

Each case: a source model (`sources`), a mutation log exactly as MutablePropertyView.exportMutations() wrote it for the edits named in `why` (ids and timestamps normalised), and the file the TypeScript StepExporter writes after importMutations(log) into a view wired like the viewer (configureMutationView).

`expected` is that file line by line, with the GlobalId of every record the export generated (express id above the source maximum) replaced by <GUID>: the one difference the two writers have by design.
Run by rust/export/tests/step_log_parity.rs and packages/export/src/step-log.parity.test.ts. Regenerate `expected` from the TypeScript exporter when its output changes on purpose; never by hand.

`refusedCases` are logs the Rust writer refuses where the TypeScript replay writes a file WITHOUT one record (`skipped` is that record's index): the TypeScript half pins that skip, the Rust half and the wasm contract pin the refusal (`error` is a substring of the message).

cases.name: update-property-in-existing-set
cases.why: UPDATE_PROPERTY inside a source set: the whole set is regenerated from base+overlay, keeping each untouched property's declared type (IFCIDENTIFIER, IFCTHERMALTRANSMITTANCEMEASURE).

cases.name: delete-property-shared-set
cases.why: DELETE_PROPERTY in a set two walls share: the TypeScript exporter withholds the shared set and its relationship, so the OTHER wall loses the set (a known data loss this port reproduces).

cases.name: create-property-new-set
cases.why: CREATE_PROPERTY into a set the entity does not have: a new set and relationship.

cases.name: create-property-set
cases.why: CREATE_PROPERTY_SET with typed members.

cases.name: delete-property-set
cases.why: DELETE_PROPERTY_SET: set, members and relationship withheld; nothing regenerated.

cases.name: delete-missing-set-is-no-op
cases.why: Deleting a set name the host does not own changes nothing and counts nothing.

cases.name: update-quantity
cases.why: UPDATE_QUANTITY: the quantity set is regenerated (description, unit and formula slots are not carried).

cases.name: create-quantity-new-set
cases.why: CREATE_QUANTITY into a set the entity does not have.

cases.name: create-quantity-set
cases.why: Whole-set CREATE_QUANTITY (createQuantitySet), no propName.

cases.name: delete-quantity
cases.why: DELETE_QUANTITY keeps the rest of the set.

cases.name: delete-quantity-set
cases.why: DELETE_QUANTITY_SET withholds the set and its relationship.

cases.name: type-owned-set-update
cases.why: A type object's own (HasPropertySets) set: regenerated without a relationship, and the type line is repointed and moved after the generated sets.

cases.name: type-owned-set-delete
cases.why: Deleting a type-owned set empties HasPropertySets to $.

cases.name: type-new-set
cases.why: A new set on a type object joins its HasPropertySets.

cases.name: attributes
cases.why: UPDATE_ATTRIBUTE: string, enum and REAL slots, a quote needing escape, and a refused non-number on a REAL slot.

cases.name: attribute-and-type-set
cases.why: A rename and a set edit on the same type object land on the one moved line.

cases.name: value-serialization
cases.why: Numbers through Number.prototype.toString: exponent forms, a REAL typed as INTEGER, unicode, a list value, NaN, and a named-member type change.

cases.name: constrained-measure-relaxes
cases.why: A value outside IfcPositiveLengthMeasure / IfcNormalisedRatioMeasure relaxes to the unconstrained ancestor; the set also carries enumerated, bounded, list, logical-unknown, vendor-typed, complex and escaped properties the regeneration collapses as the extractor does.

cases.name: same-name-sets
cases.why: Two same-named sets on one host: an edit lands on the instance that claims the member, a new member on the first instance.

cases.name: shared-atom-retained
cases.why: A regenerated set's member that another kept set also names is still written; the malformed relationship is withheld.

cases.name: owner-history-fallback
cases.why: A host with no owner history: generated sets fall back to the first one the export writes.

cases.name: ifc2x3-edits
cases.why: IFC2X3: a set regenerated with the host's own owner history; IfcDoorStyle is not read as a type object's own sets by the viewer wiring (its name does not end in Type), so its set edit takes the occurrence path.

cases.name: delete-entity-rel-cleanup
cases.why: DELETE_ENTITY: the wall is not written, list slots naming it are narrowed, and relationships naming it in a single-valued slot are withheld.

cases.name: delete-shared-member
cases.why: Deleting one of two walls sharing a set leaves the set and narrows its relationship.

cases.name: delete-set-container
cases.why: Deleting a property set itself withholds the relationship whose single RelatingPropertyDefinition named it.

cases.name: delete-owner-and-context
cases.why: Deleting records many others name: relationships withheld, owner-history fallback moves, the malformed relationship withheld.

cases.name: retype-with-predefined
cases.why: UPDATE_ENTITY_TYPE to a class whose enum has the requested member: attributes re-laid-out by name.

cases.name: retype-unknown-predefined
cases.why: An unknown PredefinedType becomes USERDEFINED with the value in ObjectType.

cases.name: retype-type-object-with-set-edit
cases.why: A retyped type object keeps its own sets repointed on the one moved line.

cases.name: retype-ifc2x3
cases.why: IFC2X3 retypes read the IFC2X3 entity table (IfcWallStandardCase -> IfcWall, IfcDoorStyle -> IfcWindowStyle).

cases.name: positional-edits
cases.why: UPDATE_POSITIONAL_ATTRIBUTE: a string, a number in a REAL slot, a list, and $.

cases.name: positional-typed-markers
cases.why: The { typed } and { real } write markers.

cases.name: create-entity-with-edits
cases.why: CREATE_ENTITY with its payload in newEntities, plus a set and a rename recorded against it: written after everything else, counted as new.

cases.name: create-relationship-naming-deleted
cases.why: A created relationship naming a deleted wall is narrowed like a source one.

cases.name: create-then-delete
cases.why: A created entity deleted in the same session is gone with its edits.

cases.name: created-type-object-owned-set
cases.why: A created type object with a set edit: the set is generated without a relationship and the created line carries it in HasPropertySets; a created retyped entity with a positional edit.

refusedCases.name: unrecognised-mutation-type
refusedCases.why: A mutation `type` this writer does not know (e.g. from a newer producer). applyMutationsBatch warns and skips it; a native save refuses rather than drop what may be an edit.

refusedCases.name: attribute-cleared-with-null
refusedCases.why: setAttribute(id, name, null) records newValue: null. The live TypeScript view then cannot export at all (serialization throws) and importMutations drops the record; neither writes the edit, so the Rust writer refuses instead of dropping it. '' clears an attribute.
